text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High p95 latency spike detected in eu-west inference cluster (model-prod-1). Rolling p95 ~1200ms, target 350ms. Paging oncall.

alex (oncall): On it. Checking routing + queue metrics now. @mira can you confirm if any deploys went out in the last 3 hours?

mira (sre): No deploys. Seeing queue backlog on pool-dedicated-eu and high replica CPU. Initiating scale: min_replicas +2.

paul (eng-runtime): Observed KV cache churn on longer sequences — runtime falling back to slower kernel paths. Preparing to switch traffic to quantized variant (model-prod-1-q3) as a low-risk mitigation.

alex (oncall): Applying routing fallback policy to smaller model variant (model-prod-1-small) to shed some load. Will keep 80/20 split initially.

incident-bot: routing policy change applied: 80% -> model-prod-1-small, 20% -> model-prod-1. Metrics stream shows immediate drop in CPU pressure.

jordan (support): Which customers are impacted? Need a list to draft customer advisories and set expectations.

mira (sre): Initial impact map: 3 customers exceeding p95 SLA thresholds: stripe-internal, partner-x, eleva-inc. No increased error rate, just elevated latency.

sam (product): ETA on recovery? Customers will ask for timeline.

paul (eng-runtime): After fallback p95 dropped to ~420ms from 1200ms. Still above goal but improving. If autoscale finishes and cache warms, we expect <350ms in ~20-30 minutes.

emily (comms): Drafting status page copy now. Proposed status page message:

```
Incident: Degraded inference latency in eu-west
Current status: Partial mitigation applied — routing fallback to smaller model and autoscaling initiated.
Impact: Customers in eu-west may experience elevated p95 latency for inference requests (observed up to ~500ms). No errors or data impact detected.
ETA: Expected recovery within 30 minutes while scale and cache warm. Next update in 15 minutes or when resolved.
Actions: Autoscale +2 replicas, routing fallback applied, cache warm-up jobs started. Support teams notified for affected accounts.
```

alex (oncall): Add note: "No data exfiltration" for compliance. Also include link to runbook and incident page.

emily (comms): Drafting customer email snippet to affected accounts:

"Hi — we’re reaching out about a temporary increase in inference latency in our eu-west region that may have affected your requests. We’ve applied routing fallbacks and are scaling capacity; we expect normal latency to return within ~30 minutes. No request failures or data exposure were observed. We’ll update you when fully recovered. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this message or contact support@redwood.com."

alex (oncall): Good. Set severity to P2 for status page and tag support leads. I'll post the status page update once emily approves.

mira (sre): Handoff plan: I'll be offline for a scheduled sync in ~10 minutes; @paul will take primary ownership for runtime mitigation and monitoring. Runbook steps executed: scaled +2, applied fallback, started cache prewarm job, verified traffic split.

paul (eng-runtime): Acknowledged, taking over monitoring. I’ll post updates at +15m and on full recovery. If latency worsens, I’ll trigger emergency scale experiment (burst +4) and revert routing.

alex (oncall): Posted status page update (incident-1777701234). @emily please send the customer notes to the impacted accounts list and paste copy in #customer-notify when ready.

incident-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1777701234

jordan (support): Notifying impacted accounts now. Support keep channel open for replies.

sam (product): Thanks team. Once stable, let’s schedule a brief post-incident to review cache policy and routing thresholds.

paul (eng-runtime): Noted — capturing kernel traces and KV cache metrics. Will attach to incident doc.

alex (oncall): Next update at 1777701320 (T+86s). Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
